transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Garcia (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Nimbus ML Eng), Jenna Ortiz (Nimbus Infra), Marcus Lee (Nimbus Head of ML)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check, is the audio ok?
[00:05] Samir: Yeah can hear you, thanks. Sorry ran a bit late, traffic.
[00:12] Alex: No worries. Agenda - Priya will run through the INT8/FP8 runs we did last week, share the perf deltas and quality spot checks, then we'll do next steps. 
[00:22] Priya: Cool, thanks Alex. So quick background - we executed two main runs: optimized INT8 quant profile across your 10k eval subset and an FP8 canonical run. Both on the same A100-like nodes, same seq lengths, batch config. Note: there's some compile flags that differ, I put them in the shared sheet.
[00:40] Marcus: Just to confirm, these were on Hosted or Dedicated?
[00:44] Priya: Good q - these were on Hosted dev nodes with our standard runtime. We also did a small Dedicated equivalence check but not a full run.
[00:54] Samir: Ok got it. What were the high level numbers?
[00:56] Priya: Summary first: INT8 reduced model memory by ~2.3x on average, peak GPU mem down ~60%; throughput up ~1.7x in some sequences because of reduced memory pressure. Latency p50 improved ~20%, p95 about 10% - p99 varied. However, we saw quality drop on ~4-6% of prompts (sensitivity set) - mainly answers with numeric precision and multi-hop reasoning where tokens are sensitive to quant noise.
[01:20] Priya: FP8 had less memory reduction - around 1.4x - but quality was much closer to baseline, only ~1-2% regressions on the same sensitivity set. Throughput gains were modest, ~1.1x, and latency improvements were smaller.
[01:36] Jenna: Are the regressions measurable in ROUGE / exact match or more subjective?
[01:40] Priya: Good point - a mix. For the golden set we measured EM drop from 86.2 to 83.5 for INT8 on that subset; ROUGE-L dropped ~1.6 points. For FP8 EM went to 85.4, ROUGE-L -0.6. Hallucination rate (as we defined in the sheet) increased for INT8 by 3.1 percentage points, FP8 by 0.8.
[02:03] Samir: Hmm that's notable - 3% hallucination bump is pretty bad for prod. Was this concentrated on any prompt types?
[02:10] Priya: Yes, mostly long-context multi-step reasoning and prompts requiring exact numbers or dates. Short, conversational answers were mostly fine.
[02:18] Marcus: Any ideas why INT8 is hitting those multi-hop cases harder?
[02:21] Priya: Likely quantization noise in attention weights and KV cache accumulation; with INT8 we see more rounding error in softmax tails and some degradation in attention distribution when sequence length grows. FP8 preserves more dynamic range so it holds up better. Also compile kernel selection can matter - we tested two kernels and saw small differences.
[02:41] Alex: Were temperature / sampling config identical? 
[02:45] Priya: Yes identical sampling, seeds fixed for deterministic eval where possible.
[02:50] Jenna: What about memory / batch sizes - do we get better gains if we tune batching more aggressively with INT8?
[02:56] Priya: Yeah you can push batching - INT8 gives headroom, so if you increase batch size you can get further throughput improvements, but latency p95/p99 may suffer; depends on your SLOs. We included a few curves in the sheet.
[03:10] Samir: Can you share the per-token cost delta roughly?
[03:13] Priya: Ballpark: INT8 reduced unit cost ~30-40% at current hourly pricing on hosted dev; FP8 around 10-15%. On Dedicated with reserved pricing the delta compresses but relative gains stay similar.
[03:26] Marcus: We care less about absolute raw token cost and more about predictable latency and quality. If FP8 gives better quality, maybe that matters more.
[03:33] Alex: Understood; tradeoff is quality vs cost. We should run your full eval set to see real impact.
[03:38] Priya: Agreed - that's our ask.
[03:40] Marcus: What did the small Dedicated check show?
[03:43] Priya: The dedicated equivalence run - we spun up a 4x GPU pool and ran ~1k prompts. Memory reductions and throughput gains were similar to Hosted, but the p99 latency was actually better on Dedicated because of co-located KV cache and lower jitter. That suggests Dedicated could mitigate some of the latency tail issues.
[04:03] Jenna: That's promising. Any infra caveats for running FP8 / INT8 in Private deployment?
[04:09] Priya: FP8 requires recent runtime and hardware support - some older GPUs need software emulation which hurts perf. INT8 works broadly but kernel availability matters. For VPC/on-prem we want to validate CUDA/cuDNN versions and driver compatibility; I added that checklist in the sheet.
[04:27] Samir: On hallucinations - can you point to a few examples?
[04:30] Priya: Sure I pulled 3 here: one where a math prompt produced an extra digit, one where a citation was invented, and one where chain-of-thought reasoning went off. I'll paste them in the doc. Note: transcription sometimes mangles proper nouns so check the sheet for exact text.
[04:50] Marcus: When you say chain-of-thought went off, do you mean it diverged early or slowly drifted?
[04:55] Priya: Diverged after step 3 - the attention on early tokens got diluted, likely due to quant rounding.
[05:02] Alex: Ok, operationally what do we recommend to Nimbus at this point?
[05:06] Priya: Run extended INT8 and FP8 on your full 50k eval set, collect metrics (EM, ROUGE, hallucination rate, token accuracy), and run a throughput/latency sweep with realistic batching. Then run a dedicated benchmark on reserved nodes to compare tails.
[05:20] Samir: For the extended run - how long will that take?
[05:23] Priya: With current resources ~18-30 hours depending on batching tradeoffs. We'll aim for 24h for the INT8 and 24h for FP8 - can parallelize a bit.
[05:32] Jenna: We'll need to schedule dataset transfer window - we can do overnight Friday.
[05:36] Priya: Great, we'll plan around that.
[05:40] Alex: A few clarifying Qs - do we need to change prompts or can we keep baseline?
[05:45] Priya: Keep baseline, we want apples-to-apples. We may add a small adversarial subset to stress the quantization.
[05:52] Samir: What about mitigations - any quick fixes to reduce hallucinations on INT8?
[05:55] Priya: A few: 1) selective layer quantization (keep first/last layers in FP16), 2) KV cache scaling tweaks, 3) beam/min sampling adjustments, 4) compile kernel selection. Those reduce regressions significantly in our experiments. We included a config diff in the sheet.
[06:13] Marcus: Selective layer sounds promising but adds complexity. Do you have perf numbers for that hybrid approach?
[06:18] Priya: Yes - hybrid (top/bottom layers FP16) gives most of INT8 memory wins (~1.9x vs baseline) while cutting regressions to ~1.5% on the sensitivity set. Throughput is ~1.5x. We have a chart.
[06:33] Jenna: If we go hybrid, any change to deployment or runtime?
[06:36] Priya: Slight config change at compile time; runtime handles it. No infra changes required.
[06:41] Samir: Good. On the Dedicated benchmark - what pool size do you recommend?
[06:45] Priya: For realistic throughput 2-4x A100 equivalent depending on expected QPS; for tail testing 4 GPUs with consistent traffic is a good start. We'll propose a matrix in the follow-up.
[06:56] Alex: Any red flags on security/compliance for running quantized models?
[07:00] Priya: Not really - quantization is model transformation, doesn't change data residency. Standard security docs apply: SOC2, encryption, audit logs. We can share the security deck again.
[07:10] Marcus: Ok sounds fine.
[07:12] Samir: One more ask - can you include a diff that shows examples where INT8 changed the answer vs baseline so we can triage by prompt type?
[07:19] Priya: Yup, that's in the examples tab. We'll expand to include categories.
[07:24] Alex: Great. Next, logistics - Alex will send pricing for the Dedicated pilot?
[07:28] Alex: Yes I'll send updated pilot pricing and a proposal for a 6-week dedicated pilot with two config options (hybrid INT8 and FP8) and credits to cover the extended runs.
[07:38] Jenna: Are there any blockers for us to start the extended runs?
[07:41] Priya: Need final eval subset and VPC peering window. Also need permission to spin up temporary dedicated nodes if you want parallel runs.
[07:50] Jenna: We'll confirm both by Friday.
[07:52] Marcus: Can we also book a deep-dive after the extended runs to review hallucination cases?
[07:56] Alex: Absolutely - plan a 60-90 min technical review.
[08:00] Samir: Thanks everyone.
[08:02] Alex: Quick recap: Priya runs extended INT8/FP8 on customer eval set; Priya will also test hybrid selective-layer config; Priya to produce full metrics sheet. Alex to send pricing and contract addendum. Nimbus to share 50k eval subset and confirm peering. We'll schedule Dedicated benchmark week of 9/22.
[08:20] Marcus: That matches our notes. Thanks.
[08:22] Jenna: Thanks, bye.
[08:24] Alex: Bye.

Notes/References: shared sheet link: (Redwood) /sheets/pilot-quantization-2025-09 (internal), examples tab includes three flagged hallucination cases; kernel flags and compile options in notes.

End of transcript.
